intro.title: About Toul Tompong Market
body: Toul Tompong Market (Russian Market) → Phnom Penh → Phnom Penh → Cambodia. Welcome to Toul Tompong Market, widely recognized as the central Toul Tompong Market. Located in the heart of Phnom Penh, Phnom Penh, Cambodia, this destination serves as a primary hub for travelers visiting the region.

Toul Tompong Market, also known as Russian Market, is one of Phnom Penh's most famous traditional markets. Visitors can explore hundreds of small shops selling handicrafts, souvenirs, clothing, jewelry, antiques and local food.
It blends everyday local life with a visitor-friendly shopping experience and Cambodian commercial culture.

history.title: History & Significance of Toul Tompong Market
body: The market is locally called Phsar Tuol Tom Pong. Its nickname "Russian Market" comes from the 1980s, when it became a favourite shopping spot for Russian and other foreign visitors.
Today it stands as a lively meeting point of local community life and Cambodian traditional trade culture.

transport.title: Location & How to Visit Toul Tompong Market in Phnom Penh
transport.intro: The market sits in the Toul Tompong area of southern Phnom Penh, about a 15–20 minute drive from the city centre and riverside. Here are the common routes from the airport and the city.

airport.title: From Phnom Penh International Airport
airport.desc: Phnom Penh International Airport (PNH) is northwest of the city, about 11–13 km from the market.
airport.taxiDesc: Buy a ticket at the official desk in the arrivals hall, or use Grab or PassApp. Route: Airport Road → Russian Federation Boulevard (St 70) → south on Monivong Boulevard → corner of St 163 and St 440. About 30–45 minutes, fare around US$12–15.
airport.tuktukDesc: Around US$8–12 and 40–60 minutes, with street views along the way — good if you are not in a rush.
airport.tip: Tip: buy your ticket or book a ride inside the arrivals hall at the official desk to avoid inflated prices outside.

modes.title: Tuk Tuk (from the city centre)
modes.desc: From the riverside (Sisowath Quay) along St 178 → St 63 → St 440 south, about 15–20 minutes — the most local way to travel.

modes.title: Taxi / Ride-hailing
modes.desc: From the centre via Monivong Boulevard or Russian Federation Boulevard south, then turn onto St 440, about 15 minutes — comfortable for families or groups.

modes.title: Motorbike / PassApp
modes.desc: A common local option, straight via St 63 or St 440, about 15 minutes — fastest and most flexible, but mind safety and sun protection.

items.q: Where is Toul Tompong Market located?
items.a: Toul Tompong Market (Russian Market) is located in Phnom Penh, Phnom Penh, Cambodia, at the corner of Street 163 and Street 440 in the Tuol Tom Pong area.

items.q: Is Toul Tompong Market free to visit?
items.a: Yes, Toul Tompong Market (Russian Market) is a public space and is free to visit year-round. There is no entrance fee.
The market is open daily from 06:00 to 16:30.

items.q: Why is it called Russian Market?
items.a: The nickname comes from the 1980s, when it became popular with Russian and other foreign visitors.
Handicrafts, souvenirs, clothing, jewelry and antique-style collectibles are popular picks.

items.q: When is the best time to visit?
items.a: Mornings are best — it is cooler and the stalls are fully stocked.

items.q: What is the rating of Toul Tompong Market?
items.a: Toul Tompong Market has a 4.1 / 5 rating based on 8,482 Google Maps user reviews, synced in September 2026.

items.q: How do I get to Toul Tompong Market from the airport?
items.a: From Phnom Penh International Airport, take a taxi or Grab via Airport Road → Russian Federation Boulevard (St 70) → Monivong Boulevard south → corner of St 163 and St 440. About 30–45 minutes drive.

amenities.title: Practical Amenities & Facilities
amenities.intro: To help you find what you need right after arriving, here is a summary of public facilities and practical information around the market. All content is provided as neutral guidance with no commercial recommendations.

items.title: Restrooms & Toilet Facilities
items.desc: Public toilets inside the market are near the central food court and at the outer corners. They are traditional basic facilities (mostly squat and some seated toilets); bring your own tissue and hand sanitizer. A small cleaning fee is charged by an attendant (about 500–1,000 KHR, roughly USD 0.1–0.25). Modern cafés and restaurants within a 2–3 minute walk generally have standard restrooms open to paying customers.
items.tip: Tip: Facilities inside the market are basic; bring small KHR change and your own tissue.

items.title: Parking & Drop-off
items.desc: Motorbikes and e-bikes can use marked roadside parking at the four main entrances (e.g. the corner of St. 163 and St. 440), managed by an attendant who issues a parking tag; pay the caretaker fee on exit (about 1,000–2,000 KHR). The surrounding streets are narrow and congested during the day, so driving to find roadside parking is not recommended; take a Tuk-Tuk or ride-hailing service and walk in from the intersection of St. 163 or St. 440.

items.title: Dining & Refreshment
items.desc: The in-market food stalls serve Khmer-style noodle soup, pork rice, fresh tropical juice and local iced coffee at low prices. The surrounding Toul Tompong (TTP) neighbourhood also has many Western cafés, vegetarian restaurants, specialty coffee shops and Asian-fusion eateries, ideal for air-conditioned, quieter meals.

items.title: Accommodation
items.desc: Toul Tompong is an established, international residential and arts district of Phnom Penh — relatively quiet and convenient. Budget guesthouses and hostels sit within a 5–10 minute walk of the market; the area also has serviced apartments and boutique hotels suited to families or longer stays.

items.title: Supermarkets & Convenience
items.desc: Several 24-hour convenience stores are scattered around the market corners for chilled drinks, sun care, wipes and snacks. A mid-size neighbourhood supermarket is about a 5-minute walk along the main road, offering imported food, toiletries and daily goods.

items.title: Fuel, EV Charging & Power
items.desc: There is no large fuel station on the market's inner streets; the nearest standard station is on a nearby main road (e.g. Mao Tse Toung Blvd or Monivong Blvd), about a 3–5 minute drive away. Public EV chargers are still rare in traditional market areas and are mostly found at large modern malls or designated service points on main roads. Most nearby cafés and restaurants offer free Wi-Fi and wall sockets for emergency charging, and some convenience stores rent power banks.

items.title: ATMs & Currency Exchange
items.desc: Cambodia widely uses US dollars (USD) and Khmer riel (KHR); small stalls inside the market usually accept cash only (small USD bills or KHR). 24-hour ATM machines from local banks are located at the main street corners and accept international cards; licensed money changers along the streets offer two-way USD/KHR exchange.
items.tip: Tip: Check banknotes for damage when exchanging, and note that small change is usually given in KHR.

weather.outroHumidNote: Humid tropical weather — stay hydrated and rest in shade whenever you can.
weather.cityMarketScenario: This is an indoor/outdoor covered city market; the risk is mainly wet floors, heat exhaustion in narrow aisles and slippery entrances.

outfit.hot_32: It's hot today — wear light, breathable cotton or linen. Avoid dark colours and long sleeves if you can.
outfit.cool_10: Cool weather — pack a warm jacket, scarf or long sleeves.
outfit.delta_over_8: Big day-night temperature swing — carry a thin jacket you can take on and off easily.
outfit.rain_general: Wear waterproof shoes or sandals you don't mind getting wet. Avoid white fabric.
outfit.wind_5_6: Wind is picking up — avoid loose, long skirts/dresses that can blow up. Hats may blow off.
outfit.wind_7: Strong wind — avoid loose clothing and anything lightweight that can blow away.

activity.rain_p60: Rain is very likely today. Prefer the covered aisles inside the market; skip long outdoor walks around the neighbourhood.
activity.light_rain: Light rain — the market is still usable but the concrete alleyways and tile floors can be slippery, take shorter steps.
activity.heavy_rain: Heavy rain. Stick to the covered main aisles and food court. Skip the narrow outdoor lanes near the gates.
activity.thunder: Thunderstorms nearby. Stay inside the covered market structure; avoid open gates, metal awnings and open-air tuk-tuk rides if possible.
activity.hot_32: Avoid walking the market between 11:00 and 14:00 when the roof traps the most heat. Come early or after 15:00.
activity.uv_5: Sun is strong today — limit the time you spend in uncovered alleys and on street crossings.
activity.clear: Beautiful sunny weather. Great for early arrival photos at the entrances and walking around the nearby local streets.
activity.overcast: Soft overcast light — perfect for photos and long walks. No harsh shadows inside or outside.

risks.heavy_rain: ⚠️ Heavy rain alert — low spots near the market gates may pool water. Avoid stepping into unknown puddles. Avoid valley-like low side streets.

risks.wind_7: ⚠️ Strong wind alert — keep away from loose signage, hanging banners and rooftop items near the market entrances. Avoid open-air tuk-tuk rides if possible.
risks.fog: ⚠️ Low visibility — expect local traffic delays. Walking near the market is fine but please watch for motorbikes carefully.

customRoutes.intro: Three travel styles plus general half-day and full-day suggestions — choose the rhythm that fits your group.

groups.title: Family & Kids Friendly
highlights: Start early (07:00) when it's cool and stalls are just opening.
Focus on the colourful handicraft section and sweets stalls first (visual appeal for kids).
Visit the food court for a mid-morning snack — choose stalls with visible cooked-to-order dishes.
Plan one rest break at an air-conditioned café nearby before the return trip.

groups.title: Photography & Nature Lovers
highlights: Arrive 06:30 for the morning light and vendor set-up scenes.
Work the alley entrances, basket-laden vendors and textile rows for texture and color.
Save the back entrance for afternoon shade and candid people shots.
Cross the street for elevated wide frames of the market exterior and surrounding rooftops.

groups.title: Low-energy & Accessible
highlights: Arrange drop-off directly at the St.163 main gate (ramp access is available there).
Concentrate on the wide central aisles and ground-level food court, skip the narrow inner lanes.
Book a tuk-tuk or taxi back to avoid long walks in the heat.
Carry a foldable stool if standing time is limited.

halfDay.title: Half Day (3–4 hours)
steps: 07:00 – Arrive, enter through the St.163 gate and explore the souvenirs & textile rows.
09:00 – Snack and cold drink break at the central food stalls.
09:45 – Walk the handicraft and jewelry sections, complete your souvenir purchases.
11:00 – Head out, arrange transport back to your hotel or next stop.

fullDay.title: Full Day (6–7 hours, with lunch)
steps: 07:00 – Morning arrival, photograph vendor setup & textile shopping.
09:30 – Coffee or breakfast at a nearby café, cool down.
10:30 – Explore handicrafts, antiques, accessories and souvenirs.
12:30 – Lunch at a local restaurant (choose a type of local Khmer eatery).
14:00 – Optional short walk around the surrounding local neighbourhood.
15:00 – Last round of shopping; wrap up and head out before closing.

visitorServices.intro: Neutral overview of common facility types available around the market area. No specific businesses are recommended; select any reputable provider that meets your needs.

items.detail: Paid public restroom facilities of various hygiene standards can be found near the main entrances and inside the food court area. Carry small change and personal hand sanitizer.

Street-side motorbike parking is available near the market gates; car parking options are limited in the immediate vicinity and are more common within a few hundred metres. Consider arriving by tuk-tuk or taxi to avoid parking difficulty.

A wide range of dining options exists around and inside the market, including open-air food courts, local eateries, casual cafés and mid-range restaurants. Choose a style of cuisine and price level that matches your preference.

Within the surrounding blocks there are guesthouses, budget hotels, mid-range hotels and serviced apartments of varying quality and price. Booking platforms and independent review sites can be used to compare options.
Local mini-marts and medium-sized supermarkets are present within short walking distance of the main gates, suitable for drinks, snacks, toiletries and basic daily necessities.

Petrol stations with basic convenience services exist along major nearby roads. EV charging infrastructure availability varies and should be checked with your accommodation or local mapping services before travel.

Multiple bank branches and currency exchange booths are located on the surrounding arterial streets. US dollars and Cambodian riel are both widely accepted, though cash is preferred for small purchases.
Mobile operator shops and SIM card resellers are available nearby; prepaid data plans are inexpensive and recommended for mapping and translation while you shop.

background.title: Why this place matters — local context
body: Toul Tompong Market sits within one of Phnom Penh's long-established residential neighbourhoods. Its commercial activity supports several thousand local livelihoods, from small stallholders to food preparers, porters and auxiliary workers, and it has operated as a daily community gathering point for multiple generations.

The building itself is a representative example of the mid-to-late 20th-century covered market architecture common across larger Cambodian towns: a concrete frame, open-sided ventilation suited to the tropical climate, and internal alley grids that allow both natural airflow and ease of movement for pedestrians and small deliveries.

Local climate and rainfall patterns — notably the southwest monsoon season from roughly June to October — shape the rhythm of the market: mornings are always busier and cooler, while wet afternoons favour the covered food court and indoor-style stalls over long exploratory walks.

legends.title: Historical memories & local stories
body: Elderly local residents often recall that in the early post-war years the site was surrounded by unpaved lanes and small wooden houses, and that the covered market building itself replaced a much simpler open-air wet market and vegetable trading yard.

The affectionate nickname "Russian Market" entered common use during the 1980s, when a small but visible number of Russian-speaking expatriates, advisers and technicians lived and worked in the city and became frequent customers — not because the market sold Russian goods, but because it was widely known as the place where imported and hard-to-find products could be reliably found.

Today's local vendors are overwhelmingly the children and grandchildren of earlier generations of stallholders. Many still specialise in the same product categories their families offered decades ago, creating a quiet but tangible continuity of craft and trade knowledge.

responsibility.title: Visitor responsibility guidelines
items: Respect the market as a working place, not only a photo backdrop: ask permission before photographing vendors at close range or their children.
Haggle politely and in good faith; a friendly smile is usually the only "rule". Do not negotiate unless you have a genuine intention to buy.
Carry out your own litter where bins are full; avoid leaving plastic bags, bottles or food packaging in the alleyways.
Dress modestly — covered shoulders and below-knee shorts or trousers are appropriate and appreciated in this family-focused community space.
Watch your belongings in crowded alleys and keep bags zipped. Report any problem to a visibly uniformed market warden or the nearest police box on the surrounding streets.
Support small local eateries and shops when possible; a large share of spending in the market goes directly to individual households in the neighbourhood.
